modules.title: Implement and manage user identities
modules.intro: This module covers the tenant itself, the people and devices in it, partners from outside, and the link to on premises Active Directory (about 20 to 25 percent of the exam). Meet **Matai Engineering**, a 600 person engineering consultancy with offices in Auckland, Christchurch and Sydney. It still runs Active Directory on premises, and it has just bought **Ridge Survey**, a 40 person firm with its own Microsoft 365 tenant. Leilani, Matai's new identity administrator, has to bring all of this under control.

lessons.title: Built-in and custom Entra roles
steps: Three parts of a role assignment

Admin power in Microsoft Entra ID comes from **role assignments**. Each has a **role definition** (the permissions), a **security principal** (a user, a role assignable group or a service principal) and a **scope** (the whole tenant, an administrative unit or a single resource such as one app registration).
Built-in roles

Built in roles cannot be edited. **Global Administrator** can do almost everything. **Privileged Role Administrator** manages role assignments and PIM. **User Administrator** manages users and groups. **Helpdesk Administrator** resets passwords for non admins. **Global Reader** sees everything but changes nothing. Leilani gives the service desk Helpdesk Administrator, not User Administrator.
Custom roles

A **custom role** is a definition you build from a list of permissions, such as the one that lets someone update an app's credentials. People assigned custom roles need **Entra ID P1**, and creating them needs at least Privileged Role Administrator. Custom Entra roles are separate from Azure RBAC custom roles, which control Azure resources.
Working out effective permissions

To see what someone can really do, open the user's **Assigned roles**. It shows each role, its scope and whether it came directly or through a group. Permissions from all active roles add together, and there are no deny assignments. A role that is only **eligible** in PIM grants nothing until it is activated.

check.q: Matai's application team needs to rotate client secrets on app registrations and nothing else. What should Leilani do?
options: Assign them the Global Administrator role
Copy Application Administrator and remove extra permissions from it
A custom role with only the credential update permission
Assign them the Cloud Application Administrator role
check.why: A custom role grants exactly the permissions needed. Built-in roles cannot be edited or trimmed in place, and both Global Administrator and Cloud Application Administrator give far more power than rotating secrets.

lessons.key: A role assignment joins a definition, a principal and a scope, built-in roles cannot be edited, and custom roles (P1) give exactly the permissions needed.

lessons.title: Administrative units
steps: Scoping admin power

Without extra setup, a Helpdesk Administrator can reset passwords for every non admin in the tenant. An **administrative unit (AU)** limits a role assignment to the users, groups and devices inside the unit. Leilani creates one AU per office so the Sydney service desk only manages Sydney staff.
When not to use them

AUs scope management only. They do not hide objects, because users can still browse the directory. They are not full isolation, which needs a separate tenant, and they are not just in time access, which is PIM. Global Administrator cannot be scoped to an AU.
Building one

Create the AU, add members by hand, by CSV or with a **dynamic membership** rule such as department equals Sydney, then assign roles scoped to it on its Roles and administrators page. AUs cannot be nested. Adding a group to an AU lets scoped admins manage the group itself, not the users inside it. Each admin with an AU scoped role needs P1.
Restricted management AUs

A **restricted management** AU goes further: tenant wide admins, including Global Administrators, cannot change its members. Only admins scoped to that AU can. It suits executive accounts. The setting must be chosen when the AU is created and cannot be changed later. Matai puts the directors' accounts in one.

check.q: Matai wants its directors' accounts protected so that even tenant wide User Administrators cannot reset their passwords. What should Leilani create?
options: A normal administrative unit scoped to directors
A role assignable group for the directors
Conditional Access requiring MFA for the directors
check.why: Restricted management AUs block tenant scoped admins from changing their members. A normal AU only adds scoped admins and blocks no one, a role assignable group is for granting roles, and MFA on the directors' sign in does not stop admins resetting their passwords.

lessons.key: Administrative units scope admin roles to a subset of objects, and restricted management AUs also block tenant wide admins.

lessons.title: Domains and company branding
steps: The initial domain

Every tenant starts with a **name.onmicrosoft.com** domain that cannot be changed or deleted. Staff should sign in with the company's own domain instead, so Leilani adds **mataieng.co.nz** as a custom domain.
Verifying a custom domain

In Domain names, add the domain, copy the TXT (or MX) value shown, create that record at the DNS registrar, then select Verify. DNS changes can take time to spread. Once verified, Leilani can make it the **primary** domain so new users default to it. A domain can be verified in only one tenant at a time.
Ridge Survey's domain

To move ridgesurvey.co.nz into Matai's tenant later, Leilani must first remove it from Ridge Survey's tenant, which means removing every user name, email address and app that still uses it. Domains can be managed (cloud sign in) or federated, for example with AD FS.
Company branding

**Company branding** customises the sign in page: background image, banner logo, colours, sign in text and links. You can add versions per browser language. On shared Microsoft sites, branding appears after the user types their username, because only then is the tenant known. Guests see their home tenant's branding.

check.q: Leilani tries to verify ridgesurvey.co.nz in Matai's tenant, but verification fails. Ridge Survey's tenant still uses the domain. What must happen first?
options: Add a second TXT record with a longer TTL
Switch the domain to federated in Matai's tenant
Make it the primary domain in Matai's tenant
Remove it, and every reference to it, from Ridge's tenant
check.why: A domain can be verified in only one directory, so it must be removed from Ridge Survey's tenant first, including user names and addresses that use it. Extra DNS records, federation or making it primary cannot get around that rule.

lessons.key: Custom domains are verified with a DNS record, can live in only one tenant, and company branding customises the sign in page.

lessons.title: Tenant, user, group and device settings
steps: Tenant properties

Tenant properties hold the name, the **country or region** (set at creation and unchangeable), the technical contact, and the privacy contact and statement link that guests see. A Global Administrator can temporarily turn on **access management for Azure resources** to get User Access Administrator over all subscriptions, for example to regain access, then turn it off.
User settings

User settings control whether ordinary users can **register applications**, create tenants or create security groups. Restricting access to the Entra admin center only hides pages from non admins, and is not a security control, because Graph and PowerShell still work.
Group settings

Group settings decide who can create groups and how owners manage requests. Microsoft 365 groups can have an **expiration** policy, where unused groups expire unless renewed, and a **naming policy** with prefixes and blocked words. Both need P1. Deleted Microsoft 365 groups can be restored for 30 days.
Device settings

Device settings decide who can **join** devices to Entra ID and who can **register** personal devices, the maximum devices per user, extra local administrators, and Windows LAPS. Microsoft recommends requiring MFA for joining through a Conditional Access user action rather than the old device setting.

check.q: Matai's staff keep registering their own apps in the tenant. Where does Leilani stop this?
options: User settings: Users can register applications
Restrict access to the Entra admin center
check.why: The Users can register applications setting controls this, and developers can be given the Application Developer role instead. Restricting the admin center only hides pages, so registration through other tools still works. Admin consent settings govern permissions, not registration.

lessons.key: Tenant properties, user settings, group settings and device settings set tenant wide defaults such as who can register apps, create groups or join devices.

lessons.title: Users and groups
steps: Creating and managing users

Users are **members** (staff) or **guests** (outsiders), and either cloud only or synced from on premises AD. A new user needs a display name, a **user principal name** on a verified domain, a password and a **usage location**, which must be set before many licences can apply. For synced users, attributes are changed in AD, because the next sync would overwrite cloud edits.
Deleting and restoring

Deleted users are **soft deleted** for 30 days and can be restored with their properties and licences. After that, or after a permanent delete, they are gone. When a Matai engineer leaves by mistake on the wrong date, Leilani restores the account in minutes.
Group types

**Security groups** grant access to apps, resources and licences and can contain users, devices, service principals and other groups. **Microsoft 365 groups** provide a shared mailbox, calendar and site for collaboration and contain users only.
Dynamic membership

Membership is **assigned** by owners or **dynamic**, worked out by a rule such as department equals Structural. Dynamic groups add and remove members automatically and cannot be edited by hand. A rule for all staff but no guests must check user type equals Member. Dynamic user groups need P1 for every member.

check.q: Leilani wants every user whose department is Structural to be added to and removed from a group automatically. What should she create?
options: A Microsoft 365 group with assigned members
An administrative unit with dynamic membership
check.why: A dynamic user group keeps membership in step with an attribute rule. An administrative unit can be dynamic but scopes admin roles rather than granting access, and role assignable groups must use assigned membership.

lessons.key: Users need a UPN and usage location, deleted users can be restored for 30 days, and dynamic groups manage membership by rule.

lessons.title: Custom security attributes and bulk operations
steps: Custom security attributes

**Custom security attributes** are business specific labels, such as a project code or clearance level, added to users and service principals. They are grouped into **attribute sets**, with types String, Integer or Boolean, and can be limited to predefined values. They can drive filtering and Azure access conditions.
Who can see them

By default even Global Administrators cannot read or assign custom security attributes. Dedicated roles do it: **Attribute Definition Administrator** creates them and **Attribute Assignment Administrator** assigns values. That keeps sensitive values away from general admins. Attribute names cannot be renamed, and definitions are deactivated rather than deleted.
Bulk operations in the portal

The Users page offers **bulk create** (members, from a CSV template with name, user name and initial password), **bulk invite** (guests), bulk delete, bulk restore and download. Leilani downloads the latest template, fills one row per user, uploads it and checks the results. Very large jobs can time out, so she splits them.
Microsoft Graph PowerShell

For repeatable automation, **Microsoft Graph PowerShell** is the supported tool, because the older MSOnline and AzureAD modules are retired. Connect-MgGraph signs in with the scopes needed, then cmdlets such as New-MgUser, Update-MgUser and New-MgGroupMember do the work, often looping over a CSV.

check.q: Leilani needs a script to create 300 Ridge Survey accounts each time a project team joins. Which tool should she use?
options: Bulk create in the admin center each time
check.why: Microsoft Graph PowerShell is the current supported tool for scripted directory tasks. MSOnline and AzureAD PowerShell are retired. Bulk create works but is manual every time, which defeats the point of a repeatable script.

lessons.key: Custom security attributes hold sensitive business labels with their own admin roles, and bulk jobs use CSV templates or Microsoft Graph PowerShell.

lessons.title: Device join and registration
steps: Why devices need identities
A device identity lets Conditional Access, Intune and single sign on recognise the device. Without one, Leilani cannot require a compliant laptop before an engineer opens project files.
Three join types

**Entra registered** suits personal phones and laptops: the user adds a work account to a device they sign in to personally. **Entra joined** suits organisation owned Windows PCs that staff sign in to with their work account, with no on premises domain needed. **Hybrid joined** PCs are joined to on premises AD and also registered in Entra ID, which needs sync and a service connection point.
Controlling join and registration

Device settings decide who may join or register devices and how many each user may have. A Conditional Access policy on the **register or join devices** user action can require MFA. Turning off registration also blocks Intune enrolment of personal devices.
Managing device objects

**Disabling** a device blocks it from authenticating and is reversible. **Deleting** removes the object and its BitLocker recovery keys and cannot be undone. Stale devices should be disabled first and deleted after a grace period. On a Windows PC, dsregcmd status shows whether it is Entra joined, domain joined or both.

check.q: A Matai laptop is reported stolen. Leilani wants to stop it authenticating immediately but keep its BitLocker key for now. What should she do?
options: Remove the device from the user's Intune enrolment
check.why: Disabling stops the device authenticating and can be reversed, while keeping its details such as BitLocker keys. Deleting removes those keys for good. Revoking the user's sessions or changing Intune enrolment does not stop the device itself authenticating.

lessons.key: Devices are Entra registered, joined or hybrid joined, and disabling a device is reversible while deleting removes it and its BitLocker keys.

lessons.title: Licence assignment
steps: Direct and group based

A licence is assigned **directly** to a user or **inherited** through **group based licensing**. Group based licensing works with security and Microsoft 365 groups, including dynamic ones, so new joiners get licences automatically. Leilani licenses a dynamic All Staff group instead of 600 individual users.
Assigning and trimming

A License Administrator assigns a product to users or groups and can turn off individual services inside it, such as a planning app Matai does not use. A user's **usage location** must be set first, or licences with location restricted services fail.
Common errors

Group licensing errors include not enough licences, conflicting service plans (such as two versions of the same email plan), dependencies, disallowed usage location and duplicate addresses. After fixing the cause, admins **reprocess** the group. Nested groups are not supported: only direct members get licences.
Changing and reporting

A directly assigned licence cannot be removed while the same licence is inherited, so remove the user from the group instead. When moving users between licensed groups, add them to the new group first, confirm, then remove them from the old one. Graph PowerShell can report licence use per product.

check.q: Matai licenses the All Staff group, which contains a nested Sydney Staff group. Sydney engineers report they have no licence. Why?
options: Licences only apply to directly assigned users
Sydney is not an allowed usage location
Nested group members do not inherit the licence
The group must be a Microsoft 365 group
check.why: Only direct members of a licensed group receive the licence, so users in a nested group miss out. Group based licensing does work for security groups, and Sydney is a valid usage location.

lessons.key: Group based licensing gives licences to direct members of a group, needs usage location set, and errors are fixed then reprocessed.

lessons.title: External collaboration and inviting guests
steps: Tenant wide guest settings

**External collaboration settings** control B2B for the whole tenant. **Guest user access** sets how much of the directory guests can see, with limited access the default. **Guest invite settings** set who may invite, from anyone to no one. **Collaboration restrictions** allow invitations to any domain, deny listed domains, or allow only listed domains.
Leave settings

Guests can be allowed to remove themselves from the tenant, but only once privacy contact information is filled in. Self service sign up through **user flows** can be enabled for apps that external people should join on their own.
Inviting guests

Guests are invited one at a time from New user, in bulk from a CSV with the email and redirect URL, or with Graph PowerShell. Sharing in Teams and SharePoint and approved access package requests also create guests. Matai invites 25 staff from a client's engineering team for a shared project.
What a guest looks like

A guest gets a user object with user type Guest and a user name with EXT in it, and stays in **pending acceptance** until they redeem the invitation by signing in with their own identity. Leilani can resend invitations to people who have not redeemed them.

check.q: Matai must only ever invite guests from three named client domains. Which setting enforces this?
options: Guest user access set to most restrictive
Guest invite settings limited to admins
Cross-tenant access settings for each client
Collaboration restrictions with an allow list
check.why: Collaboration restrictions with an allow list limit invitations to the listed domains. Guest user access controls what guests can see, invite settings control who may invite, and cross-tenant settings only cover other Entra tenants, not every domain.

lessons.key: External collaboration settings control who can invite, which domains are allowed and what guests can see, and guests stay pending until they redeem.

lessons.title: Managing external accounts and identity providers
steps: Guest properties

**User type** (member or guest) describes the relationship with your organisation, not how someone signs in, and can be changed. The **identities** property shows the guest's identity provider, such as another Entra tenant, a Microsoft account, email one time passcode or Google. **Sponsors** record who is responsible for the guest.
Resetting redemption

If a guest's email or home account changes, **reset redemption status** lets them redeem again with the new identity while keeping their object, groups and app access. Helpdesk Administrator is the least privileged role that can do it, so there is no need to delete and re invite.
Built-in identity providers

Guests can sign in with Microsoft Entra accounts, Microsoft accounts, **email one time passcode** (on by default, for anyone without another option), and Google, which needs a client ID from Google. Facebook works only for self service sign up flows, not for invitations.
SAML and WS-Fed federation

**SAML or WS-Fed identity provider federation** lets a partner's own identity system, such as AD FS, sign in their people as guests in your tenant. Leilani enters the partner's domain, the issuer, the passive sign in endpoint and the signing certificate, ideally through a metadata URL so certificates renew automatically.

check.q: A client engineer's company changed its email domain, and she can no longer reach Matai's shared site as a guest. What is the least disruptive fix?
options: Delete the guest and invite her again
Change her user type to Member
Add her new address as a proxy address
check.why: Resetting redemption keeps her object, groups and app assignments while letting her sign in with the new identity. Deleting and re-inviting loses all of that, and changing user type or adding an address does not change which identity she signs in with.

lessons.key: Guest user type and identities describe each external user, reset redemption fixes changed identities, and SAML or WS-Fed federation uses a partner's own sign in.

lessons.title: Cross-tenant access settings
steps: Per organisation control

**Cross tenant access settings** control B2B with other Microsoft Entra tenants, one organisation at a time. **Default settings** apply to every external tenant: B2B collaboration in and out is allowed, partner MFA and device claims are not trusted, and B2B direct connect is blocked.
Organisational settings
Leilani adds Ridge Survey's tenant as an organisation and overrides the defaults. She can limit inbound and outbound access to particular users, groups and apps. Per user and app scoping needs P1.
Trust settings

**Inbound trust** lets Matai accept a partner tenant's **MFA**, **compliant device** and **hybrid joined device** claims, so Ridge Survey staff are not asked for MFA twice when Matai's Conditional Access requires it. **Automatic redemption** suppresses the consent prompt, but only when both the home tenant's outbound and the resource tenant's inbound settings enable it.
B2B direct connect

**B2B direct connect** gives partner users access to **Teams shared channels** without creating guest objects. It must be set up by both tenants, and if your policies require MFA you must trust the partner's MFA. **Tenant restrictions v2** is a separate control over which outside tenants your own users may sign in to on your devices.

check.q: Ridge Survey staff already complete MFA in their own tenant, but are prompted again when opening Matai's apps. What should Leilani configure?
options: Inbound trust: accept MFA from Ridge's tenant
Turn on B2B direct connect with Ridge
A Conditional Access policy excluding guests
check.why: Trusting the partner's MFA claim in inbound trust settings lets Matai's Conditional Access be satisfied by MFA done at home. Outbound settings control Matai's own users, direct connect covers Teams shared channels, and excluding guests from policy would remove protection entirely.

lessons.key: Cross-tenant access settings control inbound and outbound B2B per organisation, trust partner MFA and device claims, and enable direct connect for shared channels.

lessons.title: Cross-tenant synchronization
steps: Keeping two tenants in step

**Cross tenant synchronisation** automatically creates, updates and removes users from a **source** tenant in a **target** tenant. It is one way and pushed from the source. Matai uses it so every Ridge Survey employee exists in Matai's tenant without manual invitations.
Set-up order

In the **target**, enable inbound user synchronisation and automatic redemption for the source. In the **source**, enable outbound automatic redemption, then create a sync configuration with the target tenant ID and test the connection. Scope it, ideally to assigned users only, review the attribute mappings, test with **provision on demand**, then start provisioning.
How users appear

Synced users are created as **external members** by default, which gives them a fuller experience than guests. Only internal members of the source are synced. Removing a user from scope soft deletes them in the target, and disabling them in the source blocks sign in in the target.
Multitenant organisations

A **multitenant organisation** groups tenants, with one owner, so Teams and Viva Engage work more smoothly across them. It does not merge tenants: each keeps its own policies and admins. Cross tenant sync needs P1 for each synced user in the source tenant.

check.q: Ridge Survey users must appear automatically in Matai's tenant and disappear when they leave Ridge Survey. Which feature fits?
options: A monthly bulk invite from a CSV
check.why: Cross-tenant synchronization provisions and deprovisions users automatically from one tenant to another. Bulk invites are manual and never remove anyone, direct connect only covers Teams shared channels, and Cloud Sync copies on premises AD into a tenant, not tenant to tenant.

lessons.key: Cross-tenant synchronization pushes users one way from source to target as external members, after both tenants enable automatic redemption.

lessons.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and Cloud Sync
steps: Two sync tools

**Hybrid identity** gives each person one identity across on premises AD and the cloud. Two tools copy AD objects to Entra ID. **Microsoft Entra Connect Sync** is a Windows service on a domain joined server. **Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync** uses light provisioning agents, with configuration held in the Entra admin center.
Connect Sync details

Connect Sync needs a full Windows Server, treated as a Tier 0 asset as sensitive as a domain controller. It syncs every 30 minutes by default. Only one server exports at a time, and a second in **staging mode** stands ready. Filtering by domain, OU or attribute decides which objects sync, and accidental delete protection stops large deletions.
Cloud Sync details

Cloud Sync agents keep an outbound connection and sync about every two minutes. Several active agents give high availability. It handles **disconnected forests**, such as Ridge Survey's AD with no trust to Matai's, and can provision cloud groups back to AD.
When Connect Sync is still needed

Connect Sync is still required for pass-through authentication and AD FS set up, advanced custom sync rules and very large directories. Both tools can run side by side for different scopes, as long as each object is synced by only one. Matai keeps Connect Sync for its main forest and uses Cloud Sync for Ridge Survey's.

check.q: Ridge Survey's on premises AD forest has no trust with Matai's forest. Which tool most easily syncs both into Matai's tenant?
options: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync in staging mode
check.why: Cloud Sync can bring disconnected forests into one tenant using light agents. Staging mode is a standby Connect Sync server, not a way to add a second forest, AD FS is federation rather than sync, and cross-tenant settings govern B2B between cloud tenants.

lessons.key: Connect Sync is a full sync server with staging mode and advanced rules, while Cloud Sync uses light agents and handles disconnected forests.

lessons.title: PHS, PTA and Seamless SSO
steps: Password hash synchronisation

With **password hash sync (PHS)**, the sync engine takes the AD password hash, adds a salt and hashes it many more times before sending it, so neither the password nor the original hash leaves the network. Entra ID then checks passwords in the cloud. Microsoft recommends it: no extra servers, sign in survives an on premises outage, and it enables **leaked credentials** detection.
Pass-through authentication

With **pass-through authentication (PTA)**, Entra ID queues the sign in and an on premises **authentication agent** checks the password against a domain controller. Agents use outbound connections only, and Microsoft recommends at least three. On premises rules such as logon hours and expired accounts apply instantly.
PTA's weakness

If every PTA agent is unreachable, sign in fails and nothing switches over automatically. Microsoft advises enabling PHS as a **backup** that admins can switch to, which also adds leaked credential detection. PTA is set up only with Connect Sync.
Seamless single sign-on

**Seamless SSO** works with PHS or PTA. It creates a computer account in AD, and browsers on domain joined devices use Kerberos to sign users in silently. It is mainly for older Windows versions, because Windows 10 and 11 joined devices use the Primary Refresh Token. Its Kerberos key should be rolled over regularly.

check.q: Matai's security policy requires that on premises logon hour restrictions apply immediately at cloud sign in. Which method fits?
check.why: PTA checks each sign in against a domain controller, so on premises restrictions such as logon hours apply immediately. PHS checks in the cloud, where logon hours are not evaluated. The other options do not use AD at all.

lessons.key: PHS checks passwords in the cloud and survives outages, PTA checks them on premises through agents, and Seamless SSO gives silent sign in on domain joined PCs.

lessons.title: Moving off AD FS and Connect Health
steps: Why leave AD FS

Many organisations used **AD FS** to federate sign in. It means servers to patch and keep available. Microsoft recommends moving to cloud authentication with PHS or PTA. Matai's AD FS farm is ageing, so Leilani plans the move.
Staged rollout

**Staged rollout** lets chosen security groups use PHS, PTA or certificate based authentication while the domain stays federated. Up to 10 groups per feature are allowed, nested and dynamic groups are not, and only synced users are in scope. Leilani starts with the IT team.
Cutting over

If Entra Connect set up AD FS, the Change user sign in option in the wizard converts the domain to PHS or PTA. Otherwise she enables the method and converts each domain to managed with Graph PowerShell. Apps that trusted AD FS are moved one by one, using the **AD FS application activity** report to see which relying parties are in use and how ready they are.
Microsoft Entra Connect Health

**Connect Health** monitors the sync service, AD FS and AD DS through agents. It shows sync errors such as duplicate attributes, AD FS usage, bad password attempts and risky IP reports, and domain controller health. It needs P1 or P2, with extra licences per additional agent, and alerts go to Global Administrators by default.

check.q: Leilani wants 50 IT staff to test password hash sync sign in before converting Matai's federated domain. What should she use?
options: Convert the domain to managed right away
Delete the AD FS farm first
A dynamic group in staged rollout
Staged rollout with an IT security group
check.why: Staged rollout moves chosen security groups to cloud authentication while the domain stays federated. Dynamic groups are not supported there, and converting the domain or removing AD FS before testing risks breaking sign in for everyone.

lessons.key: Staged rollout tests cloud authentication by group before converting a federated domain, and Connect Health monitors sync, AD FS and AD DS.

modules.title: Implement authentication and access management
modules.intro: This is the largest part of the exam (about 25 to 30 percent). It covers how people prove who they are, how Conditional Access decides what they can reach, how ID Protection reacts to risk, and how Global Secure Access replaces Matai's old VPN. Matai Engineering's engineers work on client sites with laptops and phones, so strong sign in and smart access rules matter more than the office firewall.

lessons.title: Planning authentication
steps: Weak to strong

Authentication methods range from weak (passwords, text messages) to **phishing resistant**: passkeys (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business and multifactor certificate based authentication. Planning means choosing which methods each group of users should use and moving people up that scale over time.
One policy for methods

The **authentication methods policy** is now the single place to enable each method and target it to groups. The older per user MFA and SSPR method settings are being retired, and tenants move through migration states until only the new policy is used. The **Authentication Policy Administrator** role manages it.
System preferred MFA

**System preferred MFA** prompts users with the strongest method they have registered, rather than the one they picked as default. That nudges Matai's engineers away from text messages without forcing anyone to re register.
Baseline choice

**Security defaults** are free, all or nothing protection: everyone registers Authenticator, admins always use MFA and legacy authentication is blocked. **Conditional Access** needs P1 and is fully customisable, and security defaults must be turned off to use it. Matai, with P1, uses Conditional Access.

check.q: Matai wants to enable passkeys only for the IT group first, then for everyone. Where does Leilani configure that?
check.why: The authentication methods policy enables each method and scopes it to groups. Security defaults are all or nothing, legacy per user MFA settings are being retired, and a registration campaign nudges registration of a method that must already be enabled.

lessons.key: Plan to move users toward phishing resistant methods, managed in the authentication methods policy, with Conditional Access instead of security defaults when you have P1.

lessons.title: Certificate based authentication and Temporary Access Pass
steps: Smart cards without AD FS

**Certificate based authentication (CBA)** lets Entra ID check X.509 certificates, such as smart cards, directly, without AD FS. Leilani uploads the trusted certificate authorities with their revocation list addresses, enables CBA for a group, then sets bindings. If no revocation list is set, revoked certificates are not caught.
Bindings

The **authentication binding** decides whether a certificate counts as single factor (the default) or multifactor, using rules by issuer or policy identifier. The **username binding** maps a field in the certificate to a user attribute, by default the principal name to the user principal name. Stronger, high affinity bindings use values unique to the certificate.
Temporary Access Pass

A **Temporary Access Pass (TAP)** is a time limited passcode an admin issues so a user can sign in and register a passwordless method, for example on day one or after losing a phone. Its lifetime, length and whether it is single use are configurable in the methods policy.
Who can issue it

Authentication Administrators issue TAPs for ordinary users, and **Privileged Authentication Administrators** issue them for admins. A one time TAP used to set up a passwordless method must be used within a short window. A new Matai graduate signs in with a TAP and registers a passkey before lunch.

check.q: A Matai engineer loses her phone on site and cannot sign in to register a new passkey. What should the service desk give her?
options: A one time SMS code from the service desk
check.why: A Temporary Access Pass lets her sign in for a limited time and register a new passwordless method. SSPR only resets a password and needs a registered method she no longer has, and a new user name does not prove who she is.

lessons.key: CBA validates certificates directly with authentication and username bindings, and a Temporary Access Pass bootstraps passwordless registration.

lessons.title: Microsoft Authenticator, passkeys and tenant MFA settings
steps: Authenticator settings

**Microsoft Authenticator** can allow push approvals and passwordless phone sign in. **Number matching** is always on for push, and admins can show **extra context**, the app name and location, so users spot approval requests they did not start, such as an attacker spamming prompts.
Passkeys

**Passkeys (FIDO2)** use key pairs bound to the real sign in site, so they resist phishing. **Device bound** passkeys keep the private key on one device, such as a security key or in Authenticator. **Synced** passkeys live in a provider such as a phone platform's password manager. Passkey profiles can enforce attestation and allow or block specific key models.
Tenant wide MFA settings

**Report suspicious activity** lets users report an MFA prompt they did not start, which marks them as high user risk so risk policies can act. Other tenant settings cover hardware **OATH tokens**, phone call options, and legacy options such as trusted IPs and remember MFA.
Prefer Conditional Access

Microsoft recommends Conditional Access **named locations** and **sign in frequency** over the legacy trusted IP and remember MFA settings, and remember MFA should be turned off before sign in frequency is used. Leilani removes the old trusted IP range for Matai's Auckland office and replaces it with a named location.

check.q: An engineer receives an MFA prompt at 2am that she did not start. What should she do, and what happens next?
options: Approve it, then change her password
Ask for a Temporary Access Pass
Deny it and change her phone number
check.why: Reporting marks her as high user risk, so risk based Conditional Access can force remediation. Approving lets the attacker in. Denying stops this one prompt but leaves the stolen password in use and alerts no one.

lessons.key: Authenticator uses number matching and context, passkeys are phishing resistant, and report suspicious activity raises user risk for unexpected prompts.

lessons.title: Windows Hello for Business and Entra Kerberos
steps: How it works

**Windows Hello for Business** creates a key pair on the device, ideally protected by the TPM chip, and registers the public key with Entra ID. A PIN or biometric releases it and never leaves the device, so it is phishing resistant and satisfies Conditional Access MFA requirements.
Trust types for on premises access

Hybrid users also need tickets for on premises file shares. **Cloud Kerberos trust**, recommended for hybrid, lets Entra ID issue a partial ticket that a domain controller completes, with no certificate infrastructure. **Key trust** and **certificate trust** are older options that need PKI.
Deploying it

Leilani configures Windows Hello for Business with Intune policy, or with Group Policy for domain joined PCs that Intune does not manage. Users must complete MFA before creating their PIN. Hybrid joined devices need to reach a domain controller the first time the PIN is used.
Microsoft Entra Kerberos

**Microsoft Entra Kerberos** makes cloud Kerberos trust work. Admins create a Kerberos server object in each AD domain with a PowerShell module, using Domain Admin and Enterprise Admin rights on premises and Hybrid Identity Administrator in Entra. After a passwordless sign in, users can reach on premises resources without a password.

check.q: Matai wants Windows Hello for Business on hybrid joined laptops to open on premises file shares, without building a certificate infrastructure. Which trust type fits?
check.why: Cloud Kerberos trust uses Microsoft Entra Kerberos to issue tickets and needs no PKI. Certificate and key trust both depend on certificates. PHS is a sign in method, not a Hello trust type.

lessons.key: Windows Hello for Business is phishing resistant, and cloud Kerberos trust, powered by Microsoft Entra Kerberos, reaches on premises resources without PKI.

lessons.title: Self-service password reset and password protection
steps: Turning on SSPR

**Self service password reset** is enabled for none, a selected group or all users. Admins choose how many methods are needed (one or two) and which are allowed. Users register through combined registration and can be asked to reconfirm periodically. Raising the requirement from one method to two can strand users who registered only one.
Hybrid and admins

**Password writeback**, set up through Connect Sync or Cloud Sync, writes cloud resets back to AD so the new password works everywhere. Admin accounts always use a stricter two method policy with no security questions.
Password Protection

**Microsoft Entra Password Protection** normalises each new password, fuzzy matches banned terms and the user's name, then scores it. The global banned list is always on. A **custom banned list** of up to 1,000 terms needs P1. Leilani adds Matai, the office cities and local rugby teams.
On premises and lockout

To protect AD passwords too, install the **proxy service** and the **DC agent** on every domain controller, starting in **audit** mode to see what would be blocked, then **enforced**. **Smart lockout** locks cloud sign ins after repeated failures and separates familiar from unfamiliar locations. With PTA, keep the cloud lockout threshold below AD's.

check.q: Leilani installs Password Protection agents on Matai's domain controllers and wants to see the impact before rejecting any passwords. Which mode should she start in?
check.why: Audit mode logs which passwords would fail without rejecting them, so she can judge the impact first. Enforced mode rejects passwords straight away, and smart lockout is a separate feature about failed sign ins.

lessons.key: SSPR lets users reset with registered methods and writeback keeps AD in step, while Password Protection bans weak passwords in the cloud and on premises.

lessons.title: Disabling accounts and revoking sessions
steps: Layers of blocking

When an account may be compromised or someone leaves in a hurry, blocking access has layers. **Disabling** the account stops new sign ins. For synced users, disable it in AD, because AD is the source, and Microsoft suggests resetting the AD password twice.
Revoking sessions

**Revoke sessions** invalidates refresh tokens and browser session cookies issued by Entra ID, and clears remember MFA. Without it, an attacker with a valid refresh token could keep getting new access tokens for days.
Access tokens linger

Existing **access tokens** usually last about an hour and stay valid until they expire, except in apps that support **continuous access evaluation**, such as Exchange, SharePoint and Teams, which react to the revocation almost immediately. Sessions issued by other apps must be ended in those apps.
Devices too

Leilani also disables the person's registered devices and wipes Intune managed ones if needed. Ordinary users are handled by User Administrators, admin accounts need a Privileged Authentication Administrator, and devices a Cloud Device Administrator.

check.q: A Matai account is phished. Leilani disables it, but the attacker still reads mail for a while. Which extra step cuts off existing sessions fastest?
options: Block sign in again in AD
check.why: Revoking sessions invalidates refresh tokens and session cookies, and CAE aware apps like Exchange react quickly. Removing licences, resetting MFA or blocking sign in again stop new sign ins but do not end tokens already issued.

lessons.key: Disable the account, revoke sessions to kill refresh tokens, and rely on CAE aware apps to drop access tokens quickly.

lessons.title: Planning Conditional Access and assignments
steps: How policies combine

Conditional Access evaluates signals **after first factor sign in**. Every matching policy applies: if any blocks, access is blocked, otherwise the user must meet every requirement from every policy. It needs P1, risk conditions need P2, and the least privileged admin role is **Conditional Access Administrator**.
Planning rules

Turn off security defaults first. **Exclude emergency access accounts** from every policy so a mistake cannot lock everyone out. Use a naming convention, start each policy in **report only**, and favour a few broad baselines such as MFA for everyone, MFA for admins and blocking legacy authentication.
Users and resources

**Assignments** include and exclude users, groups, roles, guests or workload identities. **Target resources** can be all resources, specific apps such as Office 365 or the Azure management API, **user actions** such as registering security info or joining devices, or an **authentication context**.
Conditions

**Conditions** add detail: user and sign in risk, **device platforms**, **locations** (named IP ranges or countries), **client apps** (including the legacy Exchange ActiveSync and other clients), **filter for devices**, and authentication flows such as device code. Matai blocks device code flow except for meeting room devices.

check.q: Two Conditional Access policies apply to a Matai engineer: one requires MFA, the other requires a compliant device. What must she do to get in?
options: Either one of the two requirements
Both MFA and a compliant device
check.why: All matching policies apply together, so every grant requirement must be met. Only a block overrides grants. Policy order and creation date do not matter.

lessons.key: All matching Conditional Access policies apply together, so plan baselines, exclude emergency accounts and start in report only.

lessons.title: Grant controls and device restrictions
steps: Grant options

Grant controls are **block access**, or grant while requiring **MFA**, an **authentication strength**, a **compliant device**, a **hybrid joined device**, an **app protection policy**, a **password change**, **risk remediation** or **terms of use**. Several controls can be combined with require all or require one.
Authentication strengths

An **authentication strength** names which method combinations count. Built in strengths are multifactor, passwordless MFA and phishing resistant MFA, and custom ones can be made. A policy cannot use require MFA and require authentication strength together. Matai requires phishing resistant MFA for admins.
Device based controls

**Compliant device** relies on Intune (or a partner MDM) marking the device as meeting policy. **Hybrid joined** accepts domain joined PCs. Using require one of the selected controls lets either pass. **Filter for devices** targets properties such as trust type or model, for example allowing admin portals only from privileged access workstations.
Unmanaged devices

For personal phones without enrolment, **app protection policy** requires Intune app protection in approved apps. **App enforced restrictions** let Exchange Online and SharePoint give a limited, browser only experience on unmanaged devices, with no download, print or sync. Matai's engineers can read drawings on their own phones but not save them.

check.q: Matai wants admins to use only phishing resistant methods, such as passkeys, when signing in to admin portals. Which grant control should Leilani use?
options: Sign in frequency set to every time
check.why: An authentication strength restricts which methods count, so phishing resistant MFA excludes text messages and push. Plain require MFA accepts any second factor, a compliant device does not limit the method, and sign in frequency controls how often, not how.

lessons.key: Grant controls block or require MFA, authentication strengths, compliant or hybrid devices or app protection, and app enforced restrictions limit unmanaged devices.

lessons.title: Session management and continuous access evaluation
steps: Default sessions
By default Entra ID uses a rolling 90 day session window, so users are not asked again while nothing changes. **Session controls** tighten this for sensitive cases.
Session controls

**Sign in frequency** forces reauthentication after a set number of hours or days, or every time. **Persistent browser session** decides whether users stay signed in after closing the browser. **Conditional Access App Control** routes sessions through Defender for Cloud Apps. **Token protection** binds tokens to the device so stolen tokens cannot be replayed elsewhere.
Continuous access evaluation

Normally access tokens live about an hour. With **continuous access evaluation (CAE)**, supporting services such as Exchange and SharePoint listen for **critical events**: the user is disabled or deleted, their password changes, sessions are revoked, or high user risk is detected. Access is cut in near real time.
Location enforcement

CAE can also enforce IP based **named locations** instantly, so a stolen token used from outside Matai's allowed networks fails. In return, CAE aware apps get longer lived tokens. Leilani must list all Matai egress addresses, including IPv6, or users may be blocked by mistake.

check.q: Matai wants engineers using the payroll app to sign in again every four hours, whatever else happens. Which control does that?
options: Persistent browser session set to always
check.why: Sign in frequency sets how often reauthentication is required. Persistent browser session would keep users signed in longer, report only mode does not enforce, and terms of use only asks for acceptance.

lessons.key: Session controls such as sign in frequency and token protection shape sessions, and CAE cuts access in near real time on critical events.

lessons.title: Authentication context and protected actions
steps: Step up inside an app

Normal policies apply when someone opens an app. An **authentication context** applies when they touch something sensitive inside it. Leilani creates a context labelled c1, publishes it to apps, then builds a Conditional Access policy targeting c1 that requires phishing resistant MFA.
Who uses authentication contexts

SharePoint sites and Teams can require a context through **sensitivity labels**. Defender for Cloud Apps session policies can require step up before a download. **PIM** can require a context when someone activates a role. Custom apps can request it too. Matai labels its tender documents site with c1.
Protected actions

**Protected actions** add step up to specific admin operations, such as creating or deleting Conditional Access policies, changing cross tenant access settings, changing named locations or hard deleting directory objects. They apply at the moment of the action, whatever role grants the permission.
Setting them up

First create an authentication context and a policy for it, excluding an emergency account. Then, under Roles and admins, protected actions, assign the context to the chosen permissions. Protected actions are not a way to block someone: role assignments still decide who may act at all.

check.q: Matai wants any admin who deletes a Conditional Access policy to have just completed phishing resistant MFA, even if they signed in hours ago. What should Leilani configure?
options: Require MFA for all admin roles
Sign in frequency of one hour for admins
A protected action with an authentication context
PIM approval for Conditional Access Administrator
check.why: Protected actions require step up at the moment of a sensitive operation, using an authentication context policy. Sign in frequency and MFA apply at sign in, and PIM approval applies at activation, so neither forces fresh authentication right before the delete.

lessons.key: Authentication contexts trigger step up for sensitive content or actions, and protected actions apply them to specific admin operations.

lessons.title: Testing policies and using templates
steps: Report only

**Report only** mode evaluates a policy on real sign ins without enforcing it. Each sign in log entry shows whether the policy would have succeeded, failed, needed user action or not applied. Leilani runs every new Matai policy this way for a week before switching it on.
What If

The **What If** tool simulates a sign in from a chosen user, app, platform, location and risk, and lists which enabled or report only policies would apply and which would not, with the reason. It is the fastest way to answer why was this person blocked.
Logs and workbooks

The **Conditional Access** tab in each sign in log shows every policy's result. With sign in logs sent to Log Analytics, the **insights and reporting workbook** shows the effect of policies across the whole organisation.
Templates

**Templates** create common policies quickly, such as MFA for admins, blocking legacy authentication or securing security info registration. They are created in report only. They exclude only the admin who creates them, so Leilani edits each to exclude the emergency accounts. Policies can be exported as JSON and imported elsewhere.

check.q: An engineer in Sydney says she is blocked from the drawings app. Leilani wants to see which policies would apply to that exact situation. Which tool should she use?
options: The audit log for the policy
check.why: What If simulates a sign in with given user, app and conditions, showing which policies would and would not apply. The audit log shows policy changes, not evaluation, Secure Score rates posture, and provisioning logs cover account sync.

lessons.key: Report only mode, the What If tool and sign in logs test policies, and templates create baseline policies quickly in report only.

lessons.title: User risk, sign-in risk and MFA registration
steps: Risk in Conditional Access

**Microsoft Entra ID Protection** (full features need P2) calculates **user risk** (is the account compromised?) and **sign in risk** (is this sign in suspicious?). The older risk policies inside ID Protection are being retired, so risk policies are built in **Conditional Access**.
User risk policy

Microsoft's recommended policy targets all users except emergency accounts and all resources, with user risk high. It requires **risk remediation** (or MFA plus a secure password change) and sign in frequency every time. Hybrid users need password writeback for this to work.
Sign in risk policy

A sign in risk policy for medium and high risk requires MFA or an authentication strength. Passing MFA proves the real user is there and **self remediates** the risky sign in. Keep user risk and sign in risk in separate policies.
Registration comes first

Users can only self remediate if they have registered MFA. A **registration campaign** nudges users to set up Authenticator or a passkey during sign in, with limited snoozes. The ID Protection **MFA registration policy** requires it. A Conditional Access policy on the **register security information** action stops attackers registering their own methods.

check.q: A Matai user who never registered MFA triggers a medium sign in risk policy that requires MFA. What happens?
options: The user is let in without MFA
The user is sent a Temporary Access Pass
check.why: Without a registered method the user cannot satisfy the MFA requirement, so access is blocked. That is why registration campaigns and the MFA registration policy matter. Risk is not dismissed or bypassed automatically.

lessons.key: Build user and sign-in risk policies in Conditional Access, and make sure users register MFA first so they can self remediate.

lessons.title: Investigating risky users, sign-ins and workload identities
steps: The reports

ID Protection has three reports: **risky users** (risk level, state and history), **risky sign ins** (detail per sign in) and **risk detections** (every detection with its type and timing). Security Reader, Security Operator or Security Administrator can view them.
Admin actions

Leilani can **confirm user compromised**, which raises risk and teaches the model, **dismiss user risk** for false positives, **reset the password**, or **block** the user. On a sign in she can confirm it safe or compromised. For a confirmed compromise she also revokes sessions and disables devices.
Risky workload identities

Apps sign in as **service principals** and can be compromised too, for example when a client secret is leaked in public code. ID Protection detects suspicious sign ins, leaked credentials and anomalous activity for service principals. Managed identities are not in scope. Full details and risk based policies need **Workload Identities Premium**.
Responding for an app

A Conditional Access policy can target workload identities and **block** service principals with high risk. To remediate, Leilani lists the app's credentials, adds a new certificate, removes the leaked secret and rotates any Key Vault secrets the app could reach. She can also disable the service principal outright.

check.q: ID Protection flags a Matai integration app because its client secret appeared on a public code site. What should Leilani do first?
options: Dismiss the risk as a false positive
Replace and remove the leaked secret
Turn on MFA for the app's owners
check.why: The leaked secret lets anyone authenticate as the app, so it must be replaced and removed. Dismissing ignores a real compromise, and changes to people's passwords or MFA do nothing to the app's own credential.

lessons.key: Use the risky users, sign-ins and detections reports to investigate, and treat leaked app credentials as compromised workload identities to rotate.

lessons.title: Global Secure Access clients and Private Access
steps: What Global Secure Access is

**Global Secure Access** is Microsoft's identity aware network access service. Traffic forwarding **profiles** decide what traffic it handles, and a **client** on each device sends that traffic to it. Matai wants to replace its ageing VPN.
The client

The Windows client runs on Entra joined, hybrid joined or registered devices (registered devices support private traffic only). It is installed by hand or through Intune and uses a light network filter rather than a VPN tunnel. Microsoft recommends disabling QUIC and DNS over HTTPS in browsers so traffic can be inspected. macOS, iOS and Android have clients too.
Microsoft Entra Private Access

**Private Access** reaches internal apps without a VPN. A **private network connector** inside the network makes outbound only connections. **Application segments** define destinations by address, name or range plus ports. **Quick Access** puts many segments in one app as a quick VPN replacement.
Per app access

For better control, Leilani creates separate **per app** enterprise applications, each with its own segments, user assignments and Conditional Access policy. The engineering file server requires a compliant device and MFA, while the timesheet server needs only MFA. Private Access needs its own licence or Entra Suite.

check.q: Matai wants engineers to reach an internal drawing server from client sites without a VPN, with a compliant device required. What should Leilani deploy?
options: Microsoft Entra Private Access, per app
A site to site VPN for each client
check.why: Private Access publishes internal apps through connectors without a VPN, and per app applications can carry their own Conditional Access. Internet Access filters web browsing, and a VPN per client is what Matai is trying to replace. Application Proxy suits web apps, not general server access.

lessons.key: Global Secure Access clients send traffic to Microsoft's edge, and Private Access uses connectors and app segments to replace VPN access to internal apps.

lessons.title: Internet Access and the Microsoft traffic profile
steps: Microsoft Entra Internet Access

**Internet Access** protects web traffic. **Web content filtering** policies allow or block by web category, domain name or URL, and when rules conflict, block wins. Policies are grouped into **security profiles** with priorities.
Applying profiles

A **baseline profile** applies to all Internet Access traffic. A Conditional Access policy that targets internet resources with the session control use Global Secure Access security profile applies a profile to chosen users. **TLS inspection** decrypts HTTPS to enforce full URL rules and needs a certificate that devices trust.
The Microsoft traffic profile

The **Microsoft traffic profile** sends Exchange Online, SharePoint and OneDrive, Teams and other Microsoft 365 traffic through Global Secure Access. Rules can forward or bypass specific destinations. If the client cannot connect, Microsoft traffic **fails open** and goes direct.
Compliant network check

To stop access from outside Global Secure Access, enable Conditional Access signalling, then create a policy that blocks every network except **all compliant network locations**. Combined with tenant restrictions, it also stops users signing in to other organisations' tenants. Matai uses it to keep project data on its own path.

check.q: Matai wants Microsoft 365 to be reachable only through its Global Secure Access path, not from any other network. What should Leilani add?
options: A web category allow rule for Microsoft 365
Enable the Microsoft traffic profile only
Block all but compliant network locations
check.why: The compliant network check uses Conditional Access to block traffic that does not arrive through the tenant's Global Secure Access. The traffic profile alone fails open, web category rules filter browsing, and office named locations would block engineers on client sites.

lessons.key: Internet Access filters web traffic with security profiles, the Microsoft profile tunnels Microsoft 365 traffic, and the compliant network check blocks other paths.

modules.title: Plan and implement workload identities
modules.intro: Software needs identities as much as people do. This module covers managed identities for Azure workloads, enterprise apps and single sign on, app registrations and permissions, and watching cloud app use with Defender for Cloud Apps (about 20 to 25 percent of the exam). Matai Engineering runs a project portal in Azure, uses a dozen SaaS tools, and still has an old on premises timesheet app, so Leilani has plenty to secure.

lessons.title: Choosing the right identity for a workload
steps: What a workload identity is

A **workload identity** is the identity software uses to authenticate: an app, a script, a virtual machine or a pipeline. Choosing the right type removes stored passwords, which are among the most common things attackers find and reuse.
Managed identities first

A **managed identity** is an Entra identity tied to an Azure resource. Azure creates and rotates its credentials, so code never handles a secret. It is the first choice for code running on Azure, such as Matai's project portal on App Service.
Service principals

A **service principal** is an app's identity in a tenant, authenticated with a certificate, a client secret or a **federated credential**. Use it for workloads outside Azure, multitenant apps and SaaS integrations. Prefer workload identity federation where the platform supports it, then a certificate, and a secret only as a last resort.
What to avoid and on premises options

A **user account** used as a service account brings password, MFA and Conditional Access problems. On premises, Windows services should use **managed service accounts**: a **group managed service account (gMSA)** can be shared by several servers and AD rotates its password automatically. Matai's old timesheet service moves to a gMSA.

check.q: Matai's project portal runs on Azure App Service and needs to read from Azure Storage. Which identity should it use?
options: A shared user account with a long password
A service principal with a client secret
check.why: Code running on an Azure resource should use a managed identity, so there is no secret to store or rotate. A service principal with a secret works but leaves a credential to manage, a user account is meant for people, and gMSAs are for on premises Windows services.

lessons.key: Use managed identities for Azure workloads, service principals with federation or certificates elsewhere, and gMSAs for on premises services.

lessons.title: Creating, assigning and using managed identities
steps: System assigned

A **system assigned** managed identity is switched on in a resource's Identity page. Azure creates an identity for that one resource, and deleting the resource deletes the identity. It cannot be shared.
User assigned

A **user assigned** managed identity is a separate Azure resource with its own lifecycle. One can be attached to many resources, and one resource can have several. Microsoft recommends them when resources are rebuilt often or many need the same access. **Managed Identity Contributor** creates them and **Managed Identity Operator** assigns them to resources.
Grant access separately

Attaching an identity grants nothing by itself. Leilani gives the portal's identity a role on the target through access control, choosing a **data plane** role such as Storage Blob Data Reader or Key Vault Secrets User. A management role such as Contributor does not let it read the data.
Getting a token

Code on a virtual machine asks the local **Instance Metadata Service** for a token for the target resource. App Service and Functions provide a similar local endpoint. Most developers simply use the Azure Identity library with DefaultAzureCredential. Anything running on that resource can request tokens, so the resource is the security boundary.

check.q: Matai's portal identity has the Contributor role on a storage account but gets access denied when reading files. What is missing?
options: A data plane role on the storage account
Managed Identity Operator on the identity
check.why: Contributor and Owner manage the storage account but do not grant access to its data. A data plane role such as Storage Blob Data Reader does. Switching identity type or giving Managed Identity Operator changes nothing about data access.

lessons.key: System assigned identities live and die with one resource, user assigned ones are shared, and either needs a data plane role on the target.

lessons.title: Enterprise app settings and admin roles
steps: What enterprise apps are

**Enterprise applications** are the service principals in your tenant: gallery SaaS apps, your own apps, Application Proxy apps and Microsoft apps. Settings exist for the whole tenant and for each app.
Tenant level settings

Tenant settings include whether users can register apps, **user consent** rules, the **admin consent workflow** and **permission classifications**. They set the guardrails that every app works within.
App level properties

Each app's properties include **enabled for users to sign in** (set to No to stop all tokens, a kill switch for a suspicious app), **assignment required** (only assigned principals can sign in) and **visible to users** (only controls the My Apps tile). Hiding an app does not block it.
Admin roles for apps

**Application Administrator** manages all apps, including Application Proxy. **Cloud Application Administrator** is the same without Application Proxy. **Application Developer** can register apps even when users cannot. An app's own **owners** can manage just that app. Leilani scopes Cloud Application Administrator to the HR app for the HR systems lead.

check.q: Matai's CRM app must be usable only by the sales team, not by everyone in the tenant. Which app setting enforces this?
options: Visible to users set to No
Owners limited to the sales team
Enabled for users to sign in set to No
check.why: Assignment required means only assigned users and groups can get tokens. Hiding the tile does not stop access, owners manage the app rather than limit who signs in, and disabling sign in would block the sales team too.

lessons.key: Tenant settings set app guardrails, assignment required restricts who can sign in, and Application or Cloud Application Administrator manage apps.

lessons.title: Microsoft Entra Application Proxy
steps: Publishing on premises apps

**Application Proxy** publishes on premises web apps to remote users without opening inbound firewall ports. A user goes to an **external URL**, Entra ID signs them in, and the request travels to a **connector** inside the network, which forwards it to the **internal URL**.
Connectors

The **private network connector** runs on Windows Server and makes outbound connections only. Microsoft advises at least two per **connector group** for availability, and groups let you place connectors close to each app's back end. The same connector serves Global Secure Access Private Access.
Pre-authentication

With **Microsoft Entra ID pre authentication**, only signed in users reach the app, and Conditional Access, MFA and Defender for Cloud Apps all apply. **Passthrough** skips that check and is rarely the right choice.
Single sign on to the back end

Application Proxy can sign users into the back end with **Kerberos constrained delegation** for Windows authentication, header based sign on, password based or SAML. Matai publishes the old timesheet app with Entra pre authentication and Kerberos SSO, so engineers on site use it without a VPN or a second password.

check.q: Matai's on premises timesheet app must be reachable from client sites with MFA enforced, and the security team will not open inbound firewall ports. What should Leilani use?
options: A public IP on the timesheet server
A site to site VPN to each client
check.why: Application Proxy uses outbound only connectors, and Entra pre-authentication lets Conditional Access require MFA. Passthrough skips Entra sign in, so MFA cannot be enforced, and a public IP or VPN means opening inbound access.

lessons.key: Application Proxy publishes on premises apps through outbound connectors, with Entra pre authentication bringing Conditional Access and MFA.

lessons.title: Integrating SaaS apps
steps: Adding an app
Leilani adds SaaS apps from the **Microsoft Entra app gallery**, which has templates for thousands of apps, or creates a non gallery app for anything else.
SSO options

**SAML** single sign on is set up with the app's identifier and reply URL, the claims to send, and a signing certificate to load into the app (watch its expiry date). **OpenID Connect** apps are usually added through consent. **Password based** SSO stores credentials for apps without federation. **Linked** is just a tile.
Provisioning with SCIM

Many apps need an account before SSO works. **Automatic provisioning** uses **SCIM**, a standard protocol, to create, update and disable accounts. Leilani enters the app's tenant URL and token, maps attributes, scopes it to assigned users and groups, tests with **provision on demand**, then turns it on.
Why SCIM beats just in time

SAML **just in time** provisioning creates an account at first sign in but never removes it. SCIM also deprovisions, so when an engineer leaves Matai, their accounts in the project management and CAD licensing apps are disabled automatically. Repeated failures put a provisioning job into quarantine until fixed.

check.q: When Matai staff leave, their accounts in a SaaS app stay active because they were created by SAML just in time provisioning. What should Leilani set up?
options: A quarterly access review of the app
check.why: SCIM provisioning updates and disables app accounts as users change or leave. Just in time provisioning only creates accounts. An access review removes the Entra assignment but does not delete the account inside the SaaS app, and session lifetime or password SSO do not manage accounts.

lessons.key: Gallery apps simplify SAML or OIDC single sign on, and SCIM provisioning creates and removes app accounts automatically.

lessons.title: Assignments, app roles and collections
steps: Assigning users and groups

On an app's Users and groups page, Leilani assigns users or groups and optionally picks one of the app's **app roles**. Group based assignment needs P1, and only direct members of an assigned group get access, because nested groups are not expanded.
App roles in the token

**App roles**, such as Reader or Approver, are defined in the app and arrive in the user's token in the roles claim, so the app can decide what they may do. Assigning an app role does not grant any directory role.
Self service and reviews

The self service page lets users request access from My Apps, optionally with approval. Access reviews can later check whether assignments are still needed. Graph PowerShell can assign app roles in bulk.
Collections in My Apps

**My Apps** shows every app a user is assigned. **Collections** group apps into tabs, such as Finance or Engineering, for chosen users and groups. A collection is a filter, not an assignment: users only see collection apps they are already assigned to. Collections need P1.

check.q: Leilani creates an Engineering collection containing the CAD licence portal, but an engineer cannot see the portal in it. What is the most likely reason?
options: She is not assigned to that app
The collection has too many apps
check.why: Collections only show apps the user is already assigned to, they never grant access. Assigning her to the app fixes it. Collections need P1, not P2, and app roles or collection size do not hide apps.

lessons.key: Assign users and groups to apps with optional app roles, and use collections to organise My Apps without granting access.

lessons.title: User and admin consent
steps: What consent is

When an app asks for permissions, such as reading a user's profile or mail, someone must **consent**. **User consent** covers only that user and only delegated permissions that do not need an admin. **Admin consent** covers the whole tenant.
User consent settings

Options are: do not allow user consent; allow it only for apps from **verified publishers** and only for permissions classified **low impact** (Microsoft's recommended setting); or allow it for any app, which is risky. **Permission classifications** mark low impact delegated permissions such as reading a basic profile.
When admin consent is needed

Admin consent is required for **application permissions** (where the app acts as itself with no user), for delegated permissions marked admin only, and for anything once user consent is turned off. Cloud Application Administrator and Application Administrator can grant most consent. Microsoft Graph application permissions need Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator.
The admin consent workflow

The **admin consent workflow** gives users a path when they cannot consent: they submit a request with a reason, and chosen reviewers approve or deny it. Being a reviewer does not itself give consent rights. Matai turns it on so engineers stop granting broad permissions to unknown apps.

check.q: Matai wants staff to be able to consent only to low risk permissions for apps from verified publishers, and to request approval for anything else. What should Leilani configure?
options: Disable user consent, with no workflow
Allow user consent for all apps
Verified publisher consent plus the workflow
Give staff the Application Developer role
check.why: Verified publisher consent with low impact classifications limits what users can approve, and the workflow gives a path for everything else. Allowing all consent is risky, disabling with no workflow leaves users stuck, and Application Developer is for registering apps, not consent.

lessons.key: Limit user consent to verified publishers and low impact permissions, and use the admin consent workflow for everything else.

lessons.title: Planning and creating app registrations
steps: Application object and service principal

An **app registration** creates an **application object** in its home tenant, a template holding the app's name, redirect addresses, credentials and requested permissions. A **service principal** is created in every tenant that uses the app, and that is where assignments, consent and Conditional Access apply.
Planning choices

Choose the **supported account types**: single tenant (most internal apps), multitenant, or including personal Microsoft accounts. Decide who may register apps, naming and ownership (at least two owners), the credential type, and delegated or application permissions. Leilani registers Matai's project portal as single tenant.
Creating and authentication settings

After registering, the overview shows the **application (client) ID**, the object ID and the tenant ID. The authentication page sets **redirect URIs** by platform: web apps, single page apps using authorisation code flow with PKCE, and mobile or desktop apps. Tokens go only to registered redirect URIs, which stops them being sent to an attacker's site. Implicit flow should stay off for new apps.
Credentials

Apps prove their identity with a **certificate** (recommended), a **client secret** (shown only once, best kept short lived and out of production) or a **federated credential**, which trusts tokens from an outside platform such as GitHub Actions so no secret is stored at all.

check.q: Matai's build pipeline in GitHub Actions needs to deploy to Azure without any stored secret. Which credential should its app registration use?
options: A federated credential for GitHub Actions
A client secret with a 24 month expiry
A certificate stored in the repository
check.why: Workload identity federation swaps GitHub's own tokens for Entra tokens, so nothing secret is stored. Secrets and certificates must both be kept somewhere, and a system assigned managed identity only works for code running on an Azure resource.

lessons.key: App registrations create an application object, service principals live in each tenant, and redirect URIs plus certificates or federated credentials secure sign in.

lessons.title: API permissions and app roles
steps: Delegated permissions
**Delegated permissions** let an app act on behalf of a signed in user. The app can only do what both the permission and the user allow. Some, such as reading the whole directory, need admin consent.
Application permissions

**Application permissions** let an app act as itself with no user, as a background job does. They always need admin consent and often reach the whole tenant, such as reading every mailbox. Requesting a permission on the registration is only a request: the grant lives on the service principal after consent.
Least privilege and your own API

Ask for the narrowest permission, such as reading the signed in user rather than all users, and remove unused ones. To expose your own API, set its Application ID URI and add **scopes** for delegated access. Application access to your API is defined with **app roles** whose allowed members are applications.
Creating app roles

An app role has a display name, allowed member types (users and groups, applications or both), a **value** that appears in the roles claim and must match the code exactly, and an enabled flag. Roles must be disabled before deletion. Matai's portal defines Project Reader and Project Approver roles.

check.q: Matai's nightly report job reads every user's calendar with no one signed in. What kind of permission does it need, and who must approve it?
check.why: With no signed in user, the job needs application permissions, and those always require admin consent. Delegated permissions need a user present, and users can never consent to application permissions.

lessons.key: Delegated permissions act for a user, application permissions act as the app and always need admin consent, and app roles define roles inside the app.

lessons.title: Cloud discovery and the cloud app catalog
steps: Defender for Cloud Apps

**Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps** is Microsoft's cloud access security broker (CASB). **Cloud discovery** compares network traffic against its **cloud app catalog** and gives each app a risk score, revealing shadow IT: cloud apps used without IT's knowledge.
Data sources

Discovery data comes from **snapshot reports** (a firewall log uploaded once), continuous reports from **Defender for Endpoint** on devices on or off the network, a **log collector** receiving logs from network appliances, or secure web gateway integrations. Matai's engineers work on client sites, so the Defender for Endpoint integration gives the best view.
Governing discovered apps

Leilani tags apps **sanctioned**, **unsanctioned** or **monitored**. With Defender for Endpoint enforcement, unsanctioned apps are blocked on devices and monitored apps show a warning users can bypass. Discovery policies can alert on newly found risky apps.
The catalog and scores
