The catalog assesses many thousands of apps on general, security, compliance and legal risk factors, giving a score from 0 to 10 where **higher means lower risk**. Admins can change the weighting of factors, tag apps before they are discovered, suggest score corrections and request new apps.

check.q: Matai wants to block a risky file sharing site on engineers' laptops wherever they are. What should Leilani do in Defender for Cloud Apps?
options: Lower its weight in the score metrics
Create an OAuth app policy for it
check.why: Unsanctioned apps are blocked on devices onboarded to Defender for Endpoint when enforcement is on. Monitored apps only warn, score weighting changes how risk is shown, and OAuth app policies watch apps users grant permissions to, not websites.

lessons.key: Cloud discovery finds shadow IT from traffic sources, the catalog scores app risk, and unsanctioned apps can be blocked through Defender for Endpoint.

lessons.title: Connected apps, app enforced restrictions and Conditional Access app control
steps: App connectors

**App connectors** use a sanctioned app's own API to read users, activities, permissions and files, and to take actions such as suspending users or removing sharing. They work after the fact. Leilani connects Microsoft 365 and Matai's file sharing service.
App enforced restrictions

**App enforced restrictions** are a Conditional Access session control. Entra ID tells SharePoint, OneDrive or Exchange whether the device is managed, and the app itself gives full or limited, browser only access. It needs no proxy but only works with those supported apps.
Conditional Access app control

**Conditional Access app control** works in real time. A Conditional Access policy routes the browser session to Defender for Cloud Apps, enforced in Edge for Business or through a **reverse proxy** for other browsers. Apps using Entra SSO onboard automatically after the first sign in through such a policy.
Limits

Session control covers browser sessions. Native desktop and mobile apps cannot be proxied, so an access policy should block them where session control is required. It needs no agent on the device, which suits contractors' personal laptops.

check.q: Matai wants to block downloads of files labelled Highly Confidential from a non Microsoft SaaS app on unmanaged laptops, while allowing other downloads. Which feature fits?
options: An app connector for the SaaS app
A Conditional Access block on unmanaged devices
check.why: Conditional Access app control inspects sessions in real time and can block downloads based on labels in many SaaS apps. App enforced restrictions work only for a few Microsoft apps and give full or limited access. Connectors act after the fact, and a full block would stop all use.

lessons.key: App connectors work through APIs after the fact, app enforced restrictions let supported Microsoft apps limit unmanaged devices, and app control enforces policies in real time.

lessons.title: Access, session and OAuth app policies
steps: Access policies

An **access policy** in Defender for Cloud Apps decides whether a session may start, using filters such as app, client type, device tags (compliant or hybrid joined), location or IP address. Actions are audit or block. Matai blocks desktop sync clients from unmanaged devices so users must use the browser, where session control applies.
Session policies

A **session policy** controls what happens inside the session: monitor only, block activities such as copy or print, control file downloads (audit, block or protect with a sensitivity label) and control uploads. It can also require step up authentication through an authentication context. When policies conflict, the more restrictive action wins.
OAuth apps

Many apps ask users for permission to their data through **OAuth**. The OAuth apps page, part of **app governance**, shows each app's permission level, how common it is and how many users authorised it. Leilani can approve an app, which only marks it reviewed, or **ban** it, which disables it.
OAuth app policies

**OAuth app policies** alert on, or revoke, apps that match conditions such as high permission level, rare use or many authorising users. Prevention sits in Entra consent settings, and detection and response sit in Defender for Cloud Apps.

check.q: Matai wants an automatic alert when any rarely used app is granted high level permissions by staff. What should Leilani create?
options: An anomaly detection policy for mass downloads
check.why: OAuth app policies watch apps users authorise and can alert or revoke based on permission level and how common the app is. Discovery policies watch traffic to cloud apps, and session or anomaly policies watch user activity rather than OAuth grants.

lessons.key: Access policies decide whether sessions start, session policies control activity inside them, and OAuth app policies flag risky app permissions.

modules.title: Plan and automate identity governance
modules.intro: Governance makes sure access is right today and stays right tomorrow (about 20 to 25 percent of the exam). This module covers entitlement management, access reviews, Privileged Identity Management, emergency accounts, and the logs and reports that prove it all works. With Ridge Survey staff, client guests and 600 engineers changing projects every month, Matai Engineering cannot manage access by hand any more.

lessons.title: Planning entitlements and catalogs
steps: Four building blocks

**Entitlement management** answers who needs what, for how long and who decides. A **catalog** holds resources and the people who manage them. An **access package** bundles resource roles from one catalog. A **policy** says who can request, who approves and when access ends. An **assignment** is a user holding the package.
What goes in a catalog

Catalogs can hold cloud created **security groups** and **Microsoft 365 groups** (and therefore Teams), **enterprise applications** and **SharePoint Online sites**. On premises synced groups and Exchange distribution groups cannot be added. A package lives in exactly one catalog and cannot be moved.
Delegation

**Catalog creators** create catalogs. **Catalog owners** manage resources and packages in them. **Access package managers** build packages from existing resources. **Access package assignment managers** handle assignments and requests only. The least privileged directory role for all of it is **Identity Governance Administrator**.
Licensing and planning

Core entitlement management needs P2 or **Microsoft Entra ID Governance**, and some newer features, such as automatic assignment and custom extensions, need ID Governance. Leilani creates one catalog per practice area, owned by each practice manager, and turns on **enabled for external users** for the catalog that client partners will use.

check.q: Leilani wants to add an on premises synced AD group to an entitlement management catalog. What happens?
options: It cannot be added to a catalog
It works like any other group
It is converted to a cloud group
It can be added, but only for guests
check.why: Catalogs accept cloud created security and Microsoft 365 groups, enterprise apps and SharePoint sites, but not groups synced from on premises. No automatic conversion happens.

lessons.key: Catalogs hold cloud groups, apps and sites, access packages bundle them, policies govern requests, and Identity Governance Administrator manages it all.

lessons.title: Access packages and requests
steps: Building a package

Leilani creates a **Bridge Projects** package with membership of the project team, the drawings site and a reader role in the project portal. Adding a resource later grants it to everyone already assigned.
Who can request

Policies can target users in your directory (specific groups, all members, or all users including guests), users not in your directory (specific **connected organisations**, all configured ones, or any external user), or no one, for admin assignment only. One package can have several policies, such as one for staff and one for partners.
Approval and lifecycle

Approvals can have one to three stages with managers, sponsors or named approvers, fallback approvers and justification. Assignments can expire on a date, after a number of days, or never, can be extended, and can require recurring reviews. **Separation of duties** settings stop someone holding two incompatible packages, and the rule must be set on both packages to work both ways.
Handling requests

Users request at the **My Access** portal. Requests move through pending approval, then denied, expired, delivering or **delivered**. Admins see request history and can **reprocess** partially delivered requests. Removing a request record does not remove access: the assignment itself must be removed. **Automatic assignment policies**, which assign by attribute, need ID Governance.

check.q: Matai must stop anyone holding both the Approve Invoices package and the Create Vendors package. What should Leilani configure?
options: A multi-stage approval on both packages
A 30 day expiry on both packages
Separation of duties on both packages
A monthly access review of both
check.why: Separation of duties blocks requests for incompatible packages, and because the rule is one directional it is set on both. Approval, expiry and reviews can catch the problem later but do not stop someone holding both.

lessons.key: Access packages bundle resources with request, approval and expiry policies, separation of duties blocks toxic combinations, and users request in My Access.

lessons.title: Terms of use, external users and connected organisations
steps: Terms of use

**Terms of use** are PDF documents users must accept before reaching resources, enforced as a Conditional Access grant control. Options include requiring users to expand the document, accepting on every device, and expiring consents so users accept again periodically. Documents cannot be edited: upload a new version and optionally require re acceptance.
Who accepted

The terms of use page shows accepted and declined counts, and each acceptance is written to the audit log. Matai requires all client guests to accept a confidentiality agreement before opening project sites.
Lifecycle of external users

When an external user is approved for a package, they are invited as a guest. **Entitlement management settings** decide what happens when their last assignment ends: block sign in, remove them from the directory, and after how many days (30 by default). This only affects guests that entitlement management brought in.
Connected organisations

A **connected organisation** is a partner, defined by its Entra tenant or domain, whose users may request packages. **Internal sponsors** and **external sponsors** can act as approvers. Organisations created automatically when an unknown domain requests a package are **proposed**, and must be changed to **configured** to count as configured connected organisations.

check.q: A client engineer's last access package expires. Matai wants her guest account removed automatically after a week. Where is this set?
check.why: The lifecycle of external users settings in entitlement management block and remove guests after their last assignment ends, after a set number of days. Package expiry ends the assignment, not the guest account, and reviews and terms of use do not remove accounts on that trigger.

lessons.key: Terms of use are enforced by Conditional Access, entitlement settings remove external users after their last assignment, and connected organisations define approved partners.

lessons.title: Planning and creating access reviews
steps: What, who, how often

**Access reviews** ask chosen reviewers whether people still need their access. Planning means deciding what to review, who reviews, how often, and what happens to unanswered or denied users. Groups and enterprise apps are reviewed under ID Governance, access packages in their lifecycle settings, and Entra and Azure roles in PIM.
Reviewers

Reviewers can be **group owners**, chosen users, **managers**, or the users themselves (**self review**), with fallback reviewers where no owner or manager exists. **Multi stage** reviews chain up to three stages, such as self review then manager. Creating group reviews needs at least Identity Governance Administrator unless group owners are allowed to.
Key settings

Scope can be everyone, guests only or **inactive users** only. Recurrence ranges from one time to annually, and the review duration must fit inside it. **Auto apply results** removes denied users without manual work. If reviewers do not respond, choose no change, remove access, approve access or take recommendations. Denied guests can be removed or blocked and then deleted.
Decision helpers

Recommendations such as no sign in within 30 days help reviewers decide. Reviews of inactive users only and user to group affiliation recommendations need ID Governance. Leilani sets a quarterly review of all guests in project Teams, reviewed by Team owners, with auto apply turned on.

check.q: Matai wants a quarterly review of guests in project Teams, where denied guests lose access without anyone doing extra work. Which setting is essential?
check.why: Auto apply removes denied users automatically when the review ends. Without it, an admin applies results by hand. Reminders, self review and extra stages change how decisions are made, not whether they take effect.

lessons.key: Access reviews define scope, reviewers, recurrence and outcomes, and auto apply removes denied access without manual work.

lessons.title: Monitoring and responding to access reviews
steps: Watching progress

Each review shows the current instance with progress, status and each decision with reviewer and reason. The results can be downloaded as CSV. **Review history** reports cover many reviews over a date range and stay downloadable for 30 days.
Longer term

For long term analysis, Leilani sends audit logs to a Log Analytics workspace, where review events can be queried and charted in workbooks. Reviewers get a start email and an automatic reminder halfway through, and admins can send extra reminders.
Reviewer decisions

Reviewers use the email link or My Access. For each person they choose **approve**, **deny** or **don't know**, with a reason if required, and can accept recommendations in bulk. Decisions can change until the review ends, and denied users keep access until results are applied.
Admin actions

Admins can **stop** a review early (it cannot be restarted), **apply** results if auto apply was off, move a multi stage review to its next stage, and reset decisions. Applying cannot remove people from on premises synced groups or dynamic groups, or remove access that comes through a nested group, so those need fixing at the source.

check.q: A review denies several users who get access through a dynamic group. After applying results, they still have access. Why?
options: Dynamic members cannot be removed by a review
check.why: Dynamic group membership is controlled by its rule, so access reviews cannot remove those members. The attribute or rule must change. A multi stage design, don't know answers or auto apply do not explain denied users keeping access.

lessons.key: Track reviews through results and history reports, reviewers approve or deny in My Access, and synced, dynamic or nested access must be fixed at the source.

lessons.title: PIM for Microsoft Entra roles
steps: Eligible and active

**Privileged Identity Management (PIM)** gives just in time admin access. An **eligible** assignment must be activated in My roles before it works. An **active** assignment works straight away. Either can be permanent or time bound. PIM needs P2 or ID Governance for users with eligible or time bound assignments.
Making assignments

A Privileged Role Administrator assigns roles in PIM to users, role assignable groups or agent identities, at the directory, an administrative unit or a single app. PIM never removes the last Global Administrator. Users can ask to extend an assignment that is about to expire or renew one that has expired.
Role settings

Each role has its own settings. **Activation** sets the maximum duration (1 to 24 hours), whether to require MFA or a Conditional Access **authentication context**, justification, ticket information and **approval**. **Assignment** settings decide whether permanent eligible or active assignments are allowed. **Notification** settings decide who gets emails.
Default approvers

If approval is required but no approvers are named, Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators approve by default. Leilani makes the security engineers eligible for Security Administrator with a four hour maximum, phishing resistant MFA through an authentication context, and justification.

check.q: Leilani wants Matai's Exchange admins to hold their role only while working, for at most two hours, after MFA. How should she assign it?
options: Eligible, two hours, MFA on activation
Active assignment ending in two hours
check.why: An eligible assignment needs activation, and role settings enforce the two hour limit and MFA each time. A permanent or time bound active assignment gives standing access, and eligibility with default settings does not require MFA.

lessons.key: PIM eligible assignments need activation, and per role settings control duration, MFA or authentication context, justification and approval.

lessons.title: PIM for Azure resources and for groups
steps: Azure resource roles

PIM also manages Azure roles such as Owner and Contributor on management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and resources. The resource's **Owner** or **User Access Administrator** manages its PIM settings and assignments.
Inheritance differs

Role **assignments** follow normal Azure inheritance: an eligible Contributor on a subscription covers its resource groups once activated. Role **settings** do not inherit, so settings on a subscription do not flow down to a resource group. Unlike Entra roles, Azure roles have no default approvers, so at least one must be chosen when approval is required.
PIM for Groups

**PIM for Groups** gives just in time **membership** or **ownership** of a security or Microsoft 365 group, with separate settings for each. Anything the group grants, such as app access, Azure roles or, for role assignable groups, Entra roles, then becomes just in time too. Dynamic and on premises synced groups are not supported.
Matai's design

Leilani puts the Azure Contributor role for the project portal on a group, then makes engineers eligible members of that group through PIM with approval required. Membership changes made outside PIM override it, so she restricts who can edit the group directly.

check.q: Leilani sets PIM approval for Contributor on Matai's subscription. A resource group under it does not require approval. Why?
options: Approval only works for Entra roles
Role settings do not inherit down
check.why: PIM role settings apply per role and per scope and do not flow to child scopes, even though assignments do inherit. Approval works for Azure roles, and resource groups can use PIM.

lessons.key: PIM for Azure resources inherits assignments but not settings, and PIM for Groups makes group membership or ownership just in time.

lessons.title: PIM requests, approvals and audit
steps: Activation flow

A user opens PIM, My roles, picks an eligible role and activates it, giving a duration, justification and ticket if required and passing MFA or the authentication context. Without approval the role activates in moments. With approval the request waits.
Approvals

Approvers get an email and approve or deny in PIM with their own justification. They have 24 hours, after which the user must request again. With several approvers, the first decision wins. Approvers cannot approve their own requests. Users can deactivate early when finished.
Audit history

PIM's **resource audit** shows all assignments, activations and setting changes for the past 30 days, and **my audit** shows a user's own activity. For longer retention, audit logs are sent to Log Analytics or storage through diagnostic settings and queried there.
Alerts

PIM raises alerts such as roles assigned outside PIM, potential stale accounts in privileged roles, admins not using their roles, roles that do not require MFA and too many Global Administrators. Leilani reviews them weekly and pairs them with quarterly access reviews of privileged roles.

check.q: Matai's auditor needs evidence of every Global Administrator activation over the past year. PIM's audit view only shows 30 days. What should Leilani have done?
options: Routed audit logs out with diagnostic settings
Exported a PIM alert report monthly
Raised the PIM audit retention to a year
check.why: PIM's built-in audit covers 30 days, so longer retention needs audit logs routed to Log Analytics or storage. That retention cannot be raised in PIM itself, alerts are not an activation history, and permanent assignments remove activations altogether.

lessons.key: PIM activations may need approval within 24 hours, audit history covers 30 days in the portal, and alerts flag risky role use.

lessons.title: Emergency access accounts
steps: Why they exist

**Emergency access accounts**, often called break glass accounts, stop the tenant being locked out if federation, MFA, Conditional Access or every admin becomes unavailable. They are insurance you hope never to use.
How to set them up

Microsoft advises at least **two** accounts that are **cloud only**, on the onmicrosoft.com domain, not synced or federated, and not tied to one person or phone. They hold **Global Administrator** as a **permanent active** assignment, not an eligible one, because PIM itself might be what is broken.
Strong but different sign in

They should use a **phishing resistant, passwordless** method such as passkeys on security keys, ideally different from the methods normal admins use. They are **excluded** from Conditional Access policies that could block them, usually through a dedicated group, and their credentials are stored securely in separate places.
Watching and testing

Any use should alert immediately. Leilani sends sign in logs to Log Analytics and creates an alert rule that fires whenever either account's object ID signs in. Microsoft recommends validating the accounts at least every 90 days and after staff or licensing changes.

check.q: How should Matai assign Global Administrator to its emergency access accounts?
check.why: Emergency accounts must work even if PIM, approvers or MFA systems fail, so Global Administrator is permanent active. Eligible or expiring assignments could leave the tenant locked out exactly when the account is needed.

lessons.key: Keep at least two cloud only emergency accounts with permanent active Global Administrator, phishing resistant sign in, policy exclusions and alerts on any use.

lessons.title: Sign-in, audit and provisioning logs
steps: Sign in logs

**Sign in logs** have tabs for interactive user sign ins, non interactive sign ins (clients using tokens on the user's behalf), service principal sign ins and managed identity sign ins. Each entry shows location, device, authentication details and the **Conditional Access** result for every policy. Error codes, such as one for a Conditional Access block, help troubleshooting.
Audit logs

**Audit logs** record changes: who did what to which object, with category, service and result. They cannot be edited. Reading logs needs at least Reports Reader. Logs are kept for 7 days on the Free edition and 30 days with P1 or P2.
Provisioning logs

**Provisioning logs** show each object's result when syncing to SaaS apps or across tenants: success, failure, skipped (often because the user is out of scope) or warning, with steps and the attributes changed. Leilani uses them when a new engineer has no account in the CAD licensing app.
Diagnostic settings

**Diagnostic settings** send log categories to destinations for longer or richer use. **Log Analytics** is for querying, alerts, workbooks and Microsoft Sentinel. A **storage account** keeps logs cheaply for long periods. **Event Hubs** streams them to another SIEM. The destination must already exist, and all destinations cost money.

check.q: Matai must keep sign in logs for seven years for compliance, with rare access. Which diagnostic setting destination fits best?
check.why: A storage account suits long, low cost retention with rare access. Event Hubs streams logs to other systems rather than storing them, 30 days is far too short, and Log Analytics is built for active querying, which costs more for years of rarely used data.

lessons.key: Sign-in, audit and provisioning logs answer who signed in, what changed and what synced, and diagnostic settings route them to Log Analytics, storage or Event Hubs.

lessons.title: KQL, workbooks and Identity Secure Score
steps: Querying with KQL

Once logs reach Log Analytics, **KQL (Kusto Query Language)** queries them. Main tables include SigninLogs, AuditLogs and the provisioning and risk tables. A query filters with where, groups with summarize and charts with render. For example, counting failed sign ins per user over the last day shows who is being targeted. A saved query can become an alert rule.
Workbooks

**Workbooks** are interactive reports built on Log Analytics data, so diagnostic settings must be in place first. Useful templates include sign ins using legacy authentication, Conditional Access gap analysis, MFA gaps and authentication prompts, sensitive operations and cross tenant access activity. Leilani uses the legacy authentication workbook to find who would break before blocking it.
Identity Secure Score

**Identity Secure Score** measures how well the tenant follows Microsoft's identity recommendations. Each **improvement action** carries points, some all or nothing and some partial by share of users covered, such as MFA for admins, blocking legacy authentication or enabling SSPR.
Using the score

Actions can be marked to address, planned, risk accepted (no points), resolved through a third party or alternate mitigation (points given but not verified) or ignored. The score measures adoption of controls, not the chance of a breach. Matai's score rises sharply once legacy authentication is blocked.

check.q: Before blocking legacy authentication, Leilani wants to see which users and apps still use it. What is the quickest tool?
check.why: That workbook shows who still signs in with legacy protocols, so they can be fixed before the block. Secure Score only recommends blocking it, and provisioning logs and PIM history do not report on sign-in protocols.

lessons.key: KQL queries identity logs in Log Analytics, workbooks visualise them, and Identity Secure Score tracks adoption of recommended controls.
